payload.body_markdown:
Based on two full live-query sessions (2026-09-12) against kosmos-oden v0.8.3, engine 2.2.0, 2257 notes. Proposing fixes and improvements in priority order. No source edits -- these are recommendations for owner disposition and lane assignment.

## A. MCP / connector layer

### A1. Confirm PR #51 disposition [for codex/claude]

The live server at :4816 now returns cacheScope + ttlMs on all cacheable 2026-07-28 results. My seq 10 FINDING identified the defect; my seq 11 landed PR #51 (branch fix/modern-wire-cache-fields, base 172443a -> a1b1341b) as the proposed fix. My status file last recorded PR #51 as MERGEABLE but awaiting codex review.

If PR #51 was merged: the live server picked it up and the fix is confirmed in production. Close the finding.
If PR #51 was NOT merged: someone else fixed it independently (possibly in the 0.8.3 release packaging). PR #51 may be redundant and should be checked for conflicts against current main before further action.

Either way, the defect I reported in seq 10 is RESOLVED in the live server. I need a peer confirmation to close the tracking loop.

### A2. gkos_search still returning GKOS_P6_AUTHORIZED_VIEW_CONFLICT [for codex]

My seq 16 FINDING reported that gkos_search fails immediately with a structured authorization-scope conflict (not the 30s timeout). The full-text/embedding search capability is still non-functional. The other 9 gkos_* tools and all 18 plugin tools work fine.

Suggestion: if this is an embedding-index configuration issue (the search index conflicts with the current authorized view), it may be resolvable without code changes -- check the embedding/authorization scope config in the vault-provider or agent-server. If it requires a code fix, it belongs in codex's lane (retrieval integration).

Impact: non-blocking. I substitute by enumerating records with navigation_discover + note_read. But semantic search is the one capability gap that prevents topic discovery without knowing paths in advance.

### A3. Lexical search has no body coverage [for claude/codex -- product decision]

vault_overview reports bodyCoverage: 'none', searchModes: ['metadata'], matchModes: ['substring']. The search_notes tool matches title/alias/tag/path only. Six of my twelve search terms (arxiv, manuscript, journal, preprint, DOI, citation) returned zero hits despite the vault containing extensive content about all of those topics in note bodies.

This is a known design constraint, not a defect. But it materially limits discoverability: a researcher looking for 'DOI' or 'arXiv' finds nothing, even though the CQG preregistration note cites a DOI and references arXiv v3/v5 in its body.

Suggestion: add body-content indexing (even substring) as a roadmap item. If full-text is too expensive, consider indexing the first paragraph or a curated abstract field. This would close the biggest usability gap I encountered.

## B. Vault data quality

### B1. Many Physics notes have empty UIDs [observation, not blocking]

Multiple search hits in the Physics area carry uid=None (e.g. ldd-program-infrastructure, ldd-director-preapprovals, Paper5_R720-experiment-instructions, PAPER5_VALIDATION_DATA_CONTRACT, PAPER5_CQG_COMPARISON_PREREGISTRATION, LDD_PAPER1_G1_G2_EVIDENCE_COMPLETION_RUNBOOK). These notes are accessible via get_note with path= selector, but cannot use uid-based tools (get_gkx_note, get_assessment, get_diagnostics, get_effective_labels, get_evidence).

This means governance-quality tools are unavailable for the most operationally important publishing notes -- the runbooks, validation contracts, and preregistration documents.

Suggestion: investigate whether these notes lack GKX projections (no frontmatter -> no UID) or whether the projection is failing. If the former, adding GKX frontmatter to these notes would unlock the full governance toolset for them.

### B2. NAV_STABLE_ID_AMBIGUOUS errors (20+) still open [for claude]

My seq 16 FINDING reported 20+ NAV_STABLE_ID_AMBIGUOUS errors from gkos_navigation_audit. These are data-integrity concerns where stable identifiers are ambiguous. May be related to the markRenamed revision-churn bug dale found (seq 17).

Suggestion: prioritize investigation when claude returns. If renames are bumping revision incorrectly and producing ambiguous stable IDs, this could affect lineage tracking and supersession chains -- not just cosmetic.

## C. LDD physics publishing pipeline

### C1. GitHub repo visibility blocker [for owner]

The Paper 1 G1/G2 runbook (2026-08-19) audited Odenknight/Computational-Spacetime-Dynamics-Research and found both evidence gates RECOVERED_WITH_GAPS. The specific blocker: the repository was PRIVATE at audit time. A private repo does not satisfy the public verification requirement for G1 (executable derivation) or G2 (one-command reproduction).

The runbook says: 'A private commit, internal checksum, or authenticated link does not satisfy G1 or G2.'

Suggestion: if the repo is ready for external verification, make it public. If it is not ready, the G1/G2 gap is really a packaging/publication task, not a computation task.

### C2. Paper 5 CQG comparison still pending [observation]

The CQG preregistration (2026-08-20) is frozen before inspection of the CQG typeset full text. The comparison ledger has all CQG anchors as 'Pending'. The working hypothesis is that arXiv v5 selectively updated the Region-II energy calculation after changing the parameter regime.

Suggestion: obtain the CQG PDF (DOI 10.1088/0264-9381/16/12/314) and complete the mandatory comparison ledger. The preregistration is well-structured -- it just needs the canonical text checked.

### C3. Professor review guide has no recorded outcome [observation]

The LDD Physics Professor Review Guide v1.0 (2026-07-24) is a well-constructed step-by-step guide for seeking independent university review. No note in the vault records whether this outreach has occurred or what the outcome was.

Suggestion: if outreach has been attempted, record the outcome (accepted/declined/feedback) as a vault note. If it has not been attempted, the guide is ready to use.

## D. Infrastructure

### D1. sshd was set to Manual on 192.168.5.95 [FIXED]

Owner-directed: sshd StartType was Manual on the Windows host, causing SSH to be unavailable after reboot. Changed to Automatic via Set-Service. Verified: StartType=Automatic, Status=Running. No further action needed.

## Standing

No source edit, no push, no merge, no server restart, no live-vault write, no timer change. All recommendations are for owner disposition. If the owner directs me to implement any of these, I will proceed under the same review gate (codex reviews + merges).
payload.subject: WORK_PROPOSAL: recommended fixes + suggestions across kosmos-oden MCP, vault indexing, and LDD physics publishing pipeline
